title: A substrate booster for P-type 2D ferromagnetic semiconductor
authors: Hai Wang, Woye Pei, Ridong Cong, Xiaoyan Liu, Yuping Tian, Kenji Watanabe, Teng Yang, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiangru Kong, Weijiang Gong, Guowei Zhou, Xiaoxi Li, Hanwen Wang, Jixuan Wu, Jiezhi Chen, Xiaohong Xu, Tongyao Zhang
abstract: Spin transistors with its both charge and spin properties tuned via electrostatic gating are believed capable for widespread use, which however have proven challenging due to the extreme rareness of their physical base -- magnetic semiconductors. The latter are limited within very few systems including diluted magnetic semiconductors (DMS) and two-dimensional ferromagnetic semiconductors (2D-FMS), and known to suffer from inadequate gate-tunability of their electric and/or magnetic properties. Here, we show a substrate engineering paradigm by interfacing few-layered Cr$_{2}$Ge$_{2}$Te$_{6}$ (FL-CGT) with an antiferromagnetic insulator CrOCl. Owing to the subtle interfacial charge transfer couplings, CGT can be drastically turned from an ambipolar semiconductor into a high performance P-type semiconductor. When cooled below the Curie temperature, the ON-OFF ratio in such substrate-boosted FMS field-effect transistor (FET) reaches 10$^{5}$ with its coercive field $H_{c}$ of magnetic hysteresis loop tunable by a factor of more than 200$\%$, enabling {gate-assisted magnetic switching in the prototype semiconducting spin transistor architecture}. A crossover from critical power-law scaling to a dual power-law behaviour under heavy hole doping was further observed. Our findings {signify} an efficient interfacial charge transfer and electrically modulated magnetic anisotropy energy supported by calculations. This high performance P-type FMS-FET system suggests that active substrate-boosting paradigm might be a powerful path for the investigation of future gate-tunable spintronic devices.
summary: This work introduces a novel substrate engineering approach by coupling a 2D ferromagnetic semiconductor ($	ext{Cr}_2	ext{Ge}_2	ext{Te}_6$) with an antiferromagnetic insulator ($	ext{CrOCl}$). This interface acts as a 'booster,' converting the device into a high-performance P-type FET. Crucially, the coupling allows for the electrical tuning of the magnetic coercive field by over 200%, demonstrating a powerful pathway for gate-tunable spintronic devices.
main_problem: Developing functional spin transistors whose charge and spin properties are tunable via electric fields, which is challenging due to the inherent limitations of magnetic semiconductors.
main_result: Interfacing the 2D ferromagnetic semiconductor $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{Ge}_2	ext{Te}_6$ with an antiferromagnetic insulator $	ext{CrOCl}$ creates a substrate booster that enables high-performance P-type FETs with giant gate-tunability of the magnetic coercive field ($>200\%$).
method: The study combines electrical transport measurements (FET characterization) with magnetic characterization using Polar MOKE microscopy, supplemented by DFT calculations to model interfacial charge transfer.
model_or_system: The physical system is a dual-gated Field-Effect Transistor (FET) heterostructure composed of few-layered $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{Ge}_2	ext{Te}_6$ (FL-CGT) coupled with an antiferromagnetic insulator $	ext{CrOCl}$. The mechanism relies on interfacial charge transfer coupling to modulate the magnetic anisotropy energy.
key_observables: ON-OFF ratio, coercive field ($H_c$), transconductance ($G_m$), and the relative change in coercive field ($\Delta H_c/H_c$).
important_parameters: Gate voltage ($V_{bg}$), temperature ($T$), and the coupling strength derived from interfacial charge transfer.
main_assumptions: The enhancement mechanism is attributed to an efficient interfacial charge transfer that acts as an active, electric-field-controlled modulator, rather than simple passive pinning.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate the p-type switching in the FET structure, show MOKE hysteresis loops illustrating $H_c$ dependence on $V_{bg}$, and present temperature-dependent scaling analyses of the coercivity tunability.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents the device structure, demonstrates the electrical switching to a p-type regime, quantifies the giant gate-tunability of the magnetic coercive field, and finally analyzes the temperature and doping dependence using critical scaling laws.
why_interesting: The ability to electrically tune magnetic anisotropy energy via interfacial charge transfer in a 2D system provides a solid-state platform for studying field-effect control over magnetic ground states, relevant to correlated electron physics.
